judgment.notes: A001: M006 takes Y=ℝ^n, K=C, codomain ℝ, f=norm; F001 supplies compactness and BG001 supplies continuity, with the standard nonempty real ordered topology and closed upper rays. Empty C causes no difficulty. A002: M005 takes the real spatial sections at fixed r∈int J and j; H002 and BG012–BG015/BG019 establish continuity, the local zero-difference-quotient argument establishes vanishing, and BG006–BG007 establish compact support. BG008–BG011 verify the finite-on-compacts product measure premise. A003 bounds each continuous absolute value on compact Q, using F003 and BG001/BG014–BG015; BG016–BG017 check its optional integral estimate. A004 uses compact Q×[3t0/4,5t0/4] (BG002), contained in the positive-time domain, and continuous |e_t|. The arbitrary extension in its binding can be zero off that domain; its restriction near this box is unchanged, so continuous-on is sufficient. Each resulting conclusion is exactly the needed real upper bound or integrability. No E applications occur.

S001 correctly instantiates H006 at t0/2 and 3t0/2. S002 obtains L even for empty C. In S003 R=max(1,L+1) satisfies R≥1 and R≥L+1>L; the coordinate norm bound puts C strictly inside Q. The compactness/interior and exact product-measure facts are checked in BG002–BG005/BG018. S004's complement is open because C is compact and Euclidean Hausdorff. At each point of its product with int J, u is constant on a neighborhood; zero difference quotients and iteration give all positive-order derivatives zero, with existence assured by H002. The finite component product/sum rules and norm-square identity in BG012–BG015/BG019 justify the regularity and vanishing of every listed scalar expression, including e_t and the differentiated flux product; no mixed-partial interchange is required. Compact support and M005 then give all integrability claims. S005's closed inner time window lies strictly inside J, so joint continuity of e_t and compactness give a bound uniform in both variables, not merely in time sections. S006's B=max(0,B0) preserves that bound and is nonnegative. t0∈int J, and arbitrariness proves the all-positive-time clause. No endpoint derivative assertion or limit/integral exchange is used.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
